origin: A short tip attached to a tool, the icons of a toolbar. It began as the name that appeared when hovering toolbar buttons whose pictures alone didn't explain them.
whenToUse: You briefly explain what an icon button means.
You explain a technical term or how something is calculated in one sentence.
The information is nice to know but not needed to finish the task.
whenNotToUse: The information is essential to the task (show it all the time).
You need interactive elements such as links or buttons.
Touch is the main way people use it.

alternatives.name: Popover
alternatives.reason: An explanation with links or buttons.

alternatives.name: Inline Validation
alternatives.reason: A hint that's always visible under a field.

accessibility: Give the tooltip role="tooltip" and connect it to the trigger with aria-describedby.
It appears at once on keyboard focus and after a short delay on hover.
Esc closes it, and it doesn't disappear when the pointer moves onto it (WCAG 1.4.13).
Give icon-only triggers their own aria-label. A tooltip is a description, not a name.
